one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 earnings very likely fall inside the window: aggregators (MarketBeat, Investing.com) list Mon 2026-10-26 after close, but as of Oct 1 Cadence has not issued its webcast notice (the Q2 notice came Jul 6, three weeks ahead), so the date is an estimate. Guidance is $1.595-1.625B revenue and $2.01-2.07 non-GAAP EPS against Zacks consensus $2.04 / $1.61B. Cadence has beaten four quarters running and the $8.1B backlog backs the quarter, so the move will come from tone on 2027, China (15% of Q2 revenue) and agent monetisation; management said H2 margins dip on Intel and Hexagon investment. The Oct 28 FOMC (supervisor-verified Polymarket 26% hike odds) also falls in the window and matters for a multiple that swung 30x-38x in September with no company news. Correction from round 1: Synopsys did not 'beat and still fall' in August. It rose 13.4% the next day ($410.00 to $464.89, Twelve Data) and only then lost 21% by Sep 15 on the rate/software selloff. So beats are rewarded on the day but give no protection against macro, and I take no directional edge from the peer read-through. Momentum (28% in 12 sessions, Synopsys investor day) and reversal risk after a near-vertical run offset. Median about $350.5, a hair below spot for some give-back of the +6.2% Oct 1 sympathy day; sigma 0.125 (above the 41%/3.5 = 11.7% norm) for the earnings gap plus FOMC; symmetric spread.

fair_value.method: 60% P/E (NTM EPS at Oct-2027 ~$10.67 on FY27 consensus $9.56, x 34x) = $363, plus 40% FCF yield (2027E FCF $7.43/share on 276M shares at 2.2%) = $338. Blend ~$353, essentially spot; supervisor corrections (FY27 $9.56, 276M shares) offset each other.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: NTM EPS at Oct 2027 (Q4'27-Q3'28) about $10.67 x 34x forward P/E

inputs_detail.derivation: Round 1 used the $9.50 midpoint of two prints; the supervisor's fact-check established StockAnalysis $9.56 (26 analysts) as the broad consensus and Zacks as a subset, so I use $9.56.

$9.56 x (0.25 + 0.75 x 1.155) = $10.67. FY2028 growth of 15.5% is a skeptic haircut to the ~16% consensus FY26-27 EPS growth (source 34); implied FY28 $11.04 matches the ~$11.0 consensus FY28. Synopsys's mid-teens revenue / mid-20s EPS CAGR model (source 27) is upside; Cadence said margins improve into 2027 (source 26).

Five-year average about 44x and spot about 41x TIKR NTM (sources 4, 39). In September the stock traded ~30x NTM at the $273.96 low (source 20) and ~37x at today's close. Synopsys trades ~25.7x its FY27 EPS guide even after re-rating to $490.54 on Oct 1 (sources 27, 41), so a 34x Cadence multiple already carries a large premium. Oppenheimer (Perform, $300) calls the stock full on 2027 earnings (source 24); TIKR's exit model uses 34x (source 39). With the 10-year near 5.3% (supervisor-verified H.15), I see no case for more than 34x and keep it as a lasting disruption and deceleration discount.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: 2027E FCF about $2.05B / 276M diluted shares = $7.43/share at a 2.2% FCF yield

inputs_detail.derivation: Midpoint of the Q2 CFO-commentary guide (source 2). Buybacks of about $200M per quarter roughly offset SBC dilution and the Hexagon share issuance (source 35). Round 1 used 275M; the supervisor flagged 276M as the guided figure.
2026 FCF of about $1.76B (OCF $2.0B less $240M capex) grown about 16%. That is consensus 2027 revenue growth of 12.9% (source 34) plus margin recovery after the H2-2026 investment period (source 26).

Spot yield on 2026 FCF is ~1.8% ($1.76B / ~$97B). I widen to 2.2% because SBC is ~9-10% of revenue (GAAP op margin 28% vs non-GAAP 45%; GAAP EPS guide $4.81 vs $8.10), so FCF overstates owner earnings (sources 1, 7, 8). Consistency check with the P/E leg: 34x is a 2.9% non-GAAP earnings yield, and FCF/share ($7.43) is ~78% of FY27 EPS, so 2.2% on FCF is the same rate stance as 34x on EPS.

bear.story: AI-agent seat compression or open-source and startup flows (Kimi K3 follow-ups now close timing at 900 MHz post-route on 45nm; ChipAgents and Cognichip are funded) start to show in 2027 renewals, and/or China (15% of revenue) worsens when the BIS Affiliates Rule suspension lapses on Jan 10, 2027, just before the Feb FY27 guide, unless the truce is extended again. Synopsys taking the marquee OpenAI and AWS deals signals share loss in IP and agents. The Feb guide lands well below the $9.56 consensus (2027 EPS ~$8.8) and the multiple compresses to ~26-27x NTM. September showed sentiment alone reaches $274 (30x), so fundamental damage puts it near $245. (The single-sourced cloud-EDA licensing rule is no longer part of this story.)

base.story: Cadence delivers roughly consensus: FY27 EPS ~$9.56, NTM ~$10.67, revenue +13%. Backlog ($8.1B), supply-constrained hardware and ~40% IP growth carry it; Synopsys's +15% FY27 guide confirms industry demand. The disruption debate and a 5%+ 10-year keep the multiple near 34x, well below the 44x five-year average.

bull.story: Agentic tools are monetised through consumption and token pricing (Synopsys now formally pitches subscription plus consumption; SemiAnalysis argues agents raise engine use), FY27 EPS beats to ~$10.0-10.3, NTM ~$11.2, and the multiple re-rates to ~42x as the 'AI loser' narrative fades, as it partly did after Synopsys's investor day.

thesis_break_reason: Unchanged at $245 (my round-1 level, now also the supervisor's). The Sep-15 close of $273.96 came on sector selling and rising yields with no company news and recovered 28% in 12 sessions, so levels in the $250s are too close to proven noise. $245 is ~7% below the $262.75 52-week low and ~25x NTM EPS at the time (~$9.8), a multiple Cadence has not sustained in a decade. Trading there would most likely mean a fundamental break: a Feb-2027 FY27 framework well below the $9.56 consensus, visible seat compression from AI agents, broad China licence losses after the Affiliates Rule suspension lapses (Jan 10, 2027), or a backlog decline.

key_uncertainties: Whether AI agents cut design-engineer seats faster than consumption and token pricing adds usage; Cadence said on Q2 that agent monetisation is 'early' with nothing in guidance
Competitive share: Synopsys won the OpenAI model partnership and the $1B+ AWS IP deal; whether Cadence's ~40% IP growth holds against that
China (15% of Q2 revenue): the BIS Affiliates Rule is suspended, not repealed, now to Jan 10, 2027, right before the Feb FY27 guide; risk deferred, not removed
Multiple under a ~5.3% 10-year: ~30x to ~37x NTM within September with no company news; Synopsys sits at ~25.7x FY27
Feb-2027 FY27 guide vs $9.56 consensus: Cadence guides conservatively (FY26 started ex-Hexagon, was cut in Q1 to absorb Hexagon, then raised back in Q2)
Insider behaviour: CEO sold ~$50M at $370-415 (May-June 2026), CFO ~$8.4M; September Form 4s are only RSU/PSU tax withholding, and no insider bought at the lows
reasoning: Round 2. I read the supervisor's file and accepted its evidenced corrections: (1) Synopsys rose 13.4% the day after its August beat (my 'beat and still fell' was wrong; verified on Twelve Data, source 41), so I dropped that base rate from the 1-month view; (2) broad FY27 consensus is $9.56 (26 analysts), giving NTM ~$10.67 at the horizon; (3) diluted shares 276M; (4) the Oct 26 date is an estimate; (5) the cloud-EDA rule stays single-sourced and is removed from my bear story; (6) the Affiliates Rule suspension was extended to Jan 10, 2027 (verified: CM Trade Law and FXStreet, sources 40, 45), which keeps China risk alive right before the Feb guide. Skeptic follow-ups: no new downgrades since round 1 beyond Weiss (Sep 25) and the WallStreetZen Hold (Sep 12); consensus PT ~$404 (low $300 Oppenheimer, high $450); a BofA '$330 to $310' cut that surfaced is from Oct 2024 and is ignored; September CEO and SVP Form 4s are tax withholding on vesting, not discretionary sales (sources 42, 43); short interest is low and slightly falling at ~1.6% of float (source 44). No short report, no new litigation, credit clean (Fitch A-). Valuation: P/E $363 (60%) and FCF $338 (40%) blend to $353 (round 1 $352). I checked the supervisor's prompt on sigma: the September 30x-38x swing was macro and is already in the 41% realised vol, so it does not justify widening on its own; but the verified rate backdrop (10y ~5.3%, 26% October hike odds) and two 9-10% headline drops in 2026 are real two-way drivers. I trim sigma from 0.38 to 0.37 rather than all the way back to 0.36. Scenarios unchanged in probability (bear $245/23%, base $363/52%, bull $470/25%; mean ~$363). Ladder: lognormal median ~$357, sigma 0.37, with a modestly fattened left tail for the China/Feb-guide cluster (P>=246 0.828 vs 0.843 lognormal) and a slightly thinned far right (multiple ceiling vs Synopsys at ~26x). Thesis break stays $245. Disagreement with the supervisor: none material; its $358 fair value is ~$5 above mine because I keep a 2.2% FCF yield for SBC. No option data, implied volatility or priors used; research was 7 searches/fetches plus one Twelve Data pull.
